Definition: from G4123; to be covetous, i.e. (by implication) to over-reach:--get an advantage, defraud, make a gain.
BiblicalUsage: Pleonekteo means to overreach, to get the advantage, to defraud. Paul says we are not ignorant of Satan's devices, lest he should get an advantage of us, in 2 Corinthians 2:11. No man is to defraud his brother in any matter, says 1 Thessalonians 4:6, and Paul asks the Corinthians, did I make a gain of you, in 2 Corinthians 12:17. He could say, we have defrauded no man, in 2 Corinthians 7:2.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Satan's oldest trick is to make me think I am getting ahead while he is getting the advantage. That is why I hold that the honest man is the only one who never loses.
